(+sparkr-dev@)

Hi Wu,

Based on the info I think you could do something along the following lines:

1) Use `take(rdd, 1)` to obtain the target point assuming 1st element in your RDD is the target.  With this, the SparkR driver node will have the two coordinates.

2) Then you could do `lapply(rdd, func)` where in func you calculate this distance between each element and the target, making use of the above coordinates directly.  (This works because closure serialization will capture the two numbers made available in the driver, and ship them to SparkR workers.)  This call returns a new RDD storing the desired distances.

If you want to learn more about Spark's programming model in general, take a look at [1].

Zongheng

[1] http://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/quick-start.html
